title: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecule
topicTitle: Average translational kinetic energy of gas molecule
notes: **Independence of gas type:** the average kinetic energy depends only on temperature, not on the mass or identity of the gas molecules. All gases at the same temperature have the same average translational KE.
**Root-mean-square speed:** $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\langle v^2 \rangle} = \sqrt{\frac{3k_BT}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$. Lighter molecules move faster on average.
**Why hydrogen escapes Earth:** at room temperature, $v_{rms}$ for H$_2$ is about 1838 m/s, which is above Earth's escape velocity (~1100 m/s at the exobase), so light gases can leak into space.
